question.problem:
The time it takes for a cab to traverse a particular avenue in a city is normally distributed with a mean of $\mu $ minutes and a standard deviation of $3$ minutes. Additionally, in $98%$ of cases, a cab traverses the avenue between $0.53\mu $ and $1.47\mu $ minutes. Find the mean time it takes for a cab to traverse the avenue, rounded to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the time it takes for a cab to traverse the avenue. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{3}^{2}),$ and we want to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.53\mu <X<1.47\mu )=0.98.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.53\mu <X<1.47\mu ) & =0.98 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.47\mu ) & =0.98 \\ P(\mu <X<1.47\mu ) & =0.49 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.47\mu ) & =0.5+0.49 \\ P(X<1.47\mu ) & =0.99\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.47\mu ) & =0.99 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.47\mu }{3}) & =0.99 \\ Φ(\frac{0.47\mu }{3}) & =0.99 \\ \frac{0.47\mu }{3} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.99)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.99)≈2.3263.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.47\mu }{3} & =2.3263 \\ 0.47\mu  & =6.9789 \\ \mu  & =\frac{6.9789}{0.47} \\  & ≈14.85.\end{aligned}
$$
